newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, more slippage seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, more slippage seen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended easier on Tuesday as players took profits from recent gains despite a strong rise in Japan's industrial output for May.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract lost 220 points to end at 20,045 after hitting a high of 20,330 on light volume of 13,065 lots.

"The revised industrial output number was better than expected so the Nikkei climbed to 20,250. But it then made a U-turn. People were locking in their profits," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.

Japan's industrial production in May rose a revised 4.5 percent from the previous month, compared with a preliminary estimate of a 3.8 percent increase, according to the Ministry of International Trade and Industry.
The dealer said the market's rally on Monday was largely a technical rebound and it was unlikely to rise much further.
"Dollar/yen stayed above 114 today but the Nikkei didn't get much support from that," he said.
He said the September Nikkei would find some support around 19,850 while the 20,300-20,400 region would continue to present a barrier.
Taiwan stock index futures gave up their early gains as Taipei shares ended sharply lower after hitting a seven-year high in opening trade.
The benchmark stock index tumbled 120.8 points to close at 9,472.74 on heavy profit-taking and concerns about central bank intervention.
The MSCI July contract on SIMEX lost 1.1 points to settle at 407.3 after hitting a high of 410.5 on volume of 2,162 lots.
Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary that players were nervous about the market's current levels and further positive news would be necessary to sustain the rally.
